subject: Hot-standby & failback playbook for EU <-> APAC private deployments
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Leclerc <sophie.leclerc@eurobank.com>, Kenji Tanaka <kenji.tanaka@apaccloud.jp>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 08:23:00 +0000
Subject: Hot-standby & failback playbook for EU <-> APAC private deployments

Hi Sophie, Kenji —

Thanks again for the call last week. Per EuroBank's ask, attached is the initial hot-standby and failback playbook for private deployments spanning the EU and APAC regions. This is focused on the private deployment model (VPC-peered / on-prem paired with Redwood Private control plane) and assumes:

- Active primary in EU (customer-managed VPC) and warm hot-standby in APAC (Redwood-managed VPC with reserved capacity).
- Data residency: primary writes stay in EU; failback must ensure all customer PII is returned/verified in EU before the APAC standby is decommissioned.

High-level steps in the attached diagram: eu-apac-hot-standby-diagram.pdf
1) Pre-failover validation: syncing KV-cache snapshot, last-write watermark, and audit-token export.
2) Traffic cutover (stepwise): DNS low-weight shift -> BGP session promotion -> tunnel re-key (if needed) -> global cache invalidation.
3) Failback: canonicalize write owner, drain APAC write lanes, rehydrate EU caches, rotate keys, verify audit trail, run data residency checksum.

Open questions for EuroBank:
- Any contractual limits on transient cross-border copies for up to 48h during failback?
- KMS key policies: can Redwood use a customer-managed key in the EU to re-encrypt snapshots during transfer, or do you require escrowed keys?

Kenji — could APACCloud's peering support BGP community tagging so we can demote APAC routes during failback windows? We want to avoid broad BGP withdraws that might affect third-party peers.

I've attached the diagram and a diff of the runbook for the APAC branch (runbook-diff.docx). If this direction looks good I'll schedule a 2-hour tabletop next week to walk through the steps and run a dry-run.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Security & Compliance PM, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Attachment: eu-apac-hot-standby-diagram.pdf (architecture diagram, 1.2MB)
Attachment: runbook-diff.docx (changes for APAC standby)
From: Sophie Leclerc <sophie.leclerc@eurobank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Hot-standby & failback playbook for EU <-> APAC private deployments

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the doc. A few clarifications before we move to a tabletop:

- Data gravity / transient copies: our legal team will only approve transient copies outside the EU for up to 24 hours unless the transfer is covered by an approved SCC/DP arrangement. Can Redwood support a <24h bound and produce automated deletion proofs?
- Re-encryption: we prefer a customer-managed KMS key (bring-your-own-key) hosted in our EU KMS. Any snapshot transferred to APAC must be re-encrypted under a short-lived session key and then deleted.
- Audit: we need an auditable trail showing exactly which objects moved, timestamps, and the operator identity. SOC2 logs alone aren't sufficient — we want a signed manifest.

I've attached our compliance questionnaire for failback scenarios; can you confirm whether the playbook satisfies sections 3.2 (transit copies) and 4.1 (KMS key control)?

Regards,
Sophie
Director, Cloud Security Operations — EuroBank
Attachment: eurobank-failback-questionnaire.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Leclerc <sophie.leclerc@eurobank.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 13:40:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Hot-standby & failback playbook for EU <-> APAC private deployments

Sophie —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick technical responses (we'll expand these in the runbook):

1) Transient copy SLA (<24h)
- We can restrict the maximum lifetime of any APAC-resident snapshot to 18 hours by default and automate deletion with an attestable deletion manifest. The runbook includes a signed manifest generation step (HMAC + operator signature) and a retention TTL enforcement on the APAC storage layer.

2) KMS and re-encryption
- Support for customer-managed KMS in EU: yes. Workflow: export snapshot -> encrypt with ephemeral session key generated by Redwood -> transport over mTLS tunnel -> upon arrival in APAC re-encrypt with customer session key placeholder and store only the ephemeral ciphertext. Before handing back to EU, we perform a re-encrypt under the customer's EU KMS and then trigger deletion of APAC copies.
- We will not hold plaintext during transit; keys never leave KMSEU. The runbook lists exact API calls and the order to avoid key exposure.

3) Audit & signed manifest
- We will produce a signed manifest for every snapshot movement with: object list blobs (SHA256), transfer start/finish timestamps, operator principal, and SKS HMAC. These manifests are stored in the customer's EU-only audit bucket and are federated into EuroBank's SIEM via the S3 connector.

4) Networking & BGP strategy (short)
- Prefer BGP community tagging for graceful demotion. Steps: 1) set DNS weight to 10% APAC; 2) advertise APAC with low-preference BGP community; 3) once drain metrics show <1% writes, withdraw APAC write routes; 4) run cache resync and validate checksums; 5) fully remove APAC instances.
- We can also implement hairpin NAT on the Redwood edge to avoid leaking EU origin IPs during the transient window.

We've captured these as concrete checklist items in the updated runbook (see link). Proposed tabletop: Wed 2027-08-04 09:00 - 11:00 CEST. Does that work?

- Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: runbook-diff.docx (includes checklist and API call examples)
From: Kenji Tanaka <kenji.tanaka@apaccloud.jp>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 01:15:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Hot-standby & failback playbook for EU <-> APAC private deployments

Hi team —

We can support BGP community tagging and scheduled route-demote windows. Two operational notes from APACCloud:

1) Our peering fabric requires 72h notice for modifying community-to-policy mappings if the change impacts upstream providers; for targeted demote (customer-specific) we can do a 24h expedited request but it requires a signed change ticket.
2) There is an egress scan requirement for any inbound snapshot coming from outside APAC; we can permit the snapshot to arrive into a quarantine bucket for up to 12h for automated scanning, but per EuroBank's <24h limit that reduces the actionable window.

Request: can Redwood own the signed change ticket template and provide it with the tabletop? Also propose a dry-run on Fri 2027-08-06 02:00 - 04:00 JST to validate the pipeline with a dummy snapshot.

Thanks,
Kenji
Network Ops Lead, APACCloud

- APACCloud (Kenji): confirm expedited 24h change ticket process and provide contact for the peering ops channel.
- Redwood (Karthik): schedule the dry-run Fri 2027-08-06 02:00 - 04:00 JST and prepare a synthetic snapshot; include automated deletion proof in the run.

Tabletop confirmed: Wed 2027-08-04 09:00 - 11:00 CEST (invite to follow). Dry-run: Fri 2027-08-06 02:00 - 04:00 JST.

Sophie — please let us know if legal needs updates to the waiver template; we'll hold the dry-run until we have explicit sign-off.

Cheers,
Olga
